source.name: fn_FormatCustomerName

assumptions: NVARCHAR(100) mapped to VARCHAR(100) - PostgreSQL VARCHAR is Unicode-capable by default
NVARCHAR(201) mapped to VARCHAR(201) for return type
Function marked as IMMUTABLE since it has no side effects and returns consistent results for same inputs
ISNULL() converted to COALESCE() - functionally equivalent
String concatenation operator '+' converted to '||' (PostgreSQL standard)
Parameter names prefixed with 'p_' to follow PostgreSQL naming conventions
SQL Server SCHEMABINDING not applicable - PostgreSQL functions reference objects by name resolution at runtime

reviewFlags.reason: Verify that VARCHAR(201) is sufficient for the concatenated result. The original calculation (100 + 100 + 1 for comma-space) assumes maximum length, but actual UTF-8 character encoding may differ between SQL Server and PostgreSQL in edge cases.

Confirm that empty string handling matches business requirements. If both parameters are NULL, this returns ', ' (comma-space). Consider if this is the desired behavior versus returning NULL or empty string.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server NVARCHAR uses UTF-16 encoding while PostgreSQL VARCHAR uses UTF-8. For most common characters this is transparent, but byte-level operations or length calculations may differ for certain Unicode characters.
Both ISNULL and COALESCE behave identically for this use case, but COALESCE is SQL standard and can accept more than 2 arguments if future modifications are needed.
Marked as IMMUTABLE (equivalent to SQL Server deterministic functions) to allow use in indexes and optimization. This is appropriate since the function has no database access or side effects.
